project.name: @kehto/shell
project.summary: The browser side of the Kehto runtime, written in TypeScript. A host web page uses it to load napplets (small sandboxed web apps published on Nostr) into locked-down iframes, talk to each one over its own private message channel, ask the user before granting sensitive permissions, and pass approved requests to @kehto/runtime, which does the protocol work.

nodes.label: Entry point and types
nodes.summary: The package's single entry point and the shapes a host fills in to plug its own relays, signer, windows and services into the shell.

nodes.label: Napplet message bridge
nodes.summary: Accepts each napplet's one-time hello, ties its verified identity to a private message channel, and routes its messages to the runtime and back.

nodes.label: Private channel per napplet
nodes.summary: Binds each napplet frame to the message port it hands over, and cuts it off if the frame is reloaded, says hello twice or closes the port.

nodes.label: Host hooks translator
nodes.summary: Turns the host page's browser-facing hooks (relays, signer, storage, windows) into the plain interface the runtime expects.

nodes.label: Startup handshake
nodes.summary: Answers a napplet's ready signal with the list of services the host really offers, so napplets never see a promise the runtime can't keep.

nodes.label: Napplet page preparation
nodes.summary: Prepares a napplet's verified HTML before it runs: adds the built-in window.napplet helpers, a strict content security policy and frame rules, without changing the signed bytes.

nodes.label: In-napplet helper script
nodes.summary: Generates the self-contained script injected ahead of the napplet's own code that gives it window.napplet and talks over its private channel.

nodes.label: Sandbox rules
nodes.summary: Builds the security policy and frame rules that stop a napplet reaching the network directly, opening nested frames or using game controllers.

nodes.label: Permission prompts
nodes.summary: Admits a napplet page only after its required permissions are settled, and shows the user a ready-made dialog to allow or deny each request.

nodes.label: Host records and helpers
nodes.summary: Shared records the bridge relies on (which frame is which napplet and what it may do), plus small optional proxies that pass single-domain requests to the runtime.

nodes.label: Napplet records
nodes.summary: Remembers which frame is which napplet, its sign-in key, its granted permissions, verified build hashes and which windows are playing audio.

nodes.label: Service proxies
nodes.summary: Small per-domain helpers for identity, theme, keys, media and notifications that pass napplet requests to the runtime.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Automatic checks for the bridge, page preparation, permission prompts and handshake, plus shared fake-frame helpers.

nodes.label: Kehto runtime packages
nodes.summary: The protocol engine and its siblings (permissions, request caps, reference services, Paja) that the shell hands approved messages to.

nodes.label: Napplet protocol types
nodes.summary: The shared napplet message and NAP domain definitions published by the @napplet project.

flows.title: Launch a napplet
flows.description: From verified bytes to a napplet that can send its first request.

steps.note: The host passes the verified page; required permissions are settled, asking the user if needed.
The page gets the window.napplet helper script and strict sandbox rules added in front of its own code.
Once loaded, the napplet hands over one private message port and the shell ties its identity to it.
The napplet says it's ready and is told which services the host offers.
From then on each request arriving on that port is routed onward.
The runtime checks permissions and runs the request, replying over the same port.

tour.title: The heart of the shell
tour.note: Every napplet message comes through here, on a private channel tied to a verified identity.

tour.title: Before the napplet runs

tour.note: Approved requests are handed to the Kehto runtime, which this package wraps for browsers.
